wwmc.configuration.title: Villager Colonies Settings
Claim size, citizen limits and emerald prices for town and station upgrades.
wwmc.configuration.category.workers.tool: Quarry workers before emerald crew upgrades. Every other job block has exactly one worker; add more stations to expand production or defense.
wwmc.configuration.category.mining.toolt: Mine depth, tunnel layout, quarry depth and the delay between ore-vein yields.
wwmc.configuration.category.food.tooltip: Harvest speed and the time between regular meals. Hover a setting to see the time conversion.
wwmc.configuration.category.enchanting.t: How long enchanters work and the highest enchanting level they can reach.
wwmc.configuration.category.defense.tool: The alarm threshold, automatic enemy attacks and wave size scaling.
wwmc.configuration.category.other.toolti: Additional settings that do not yet have a dedicated section.
wwmc.configuration.settlementRadius.tool: Horizontal distance from the banner to each edge of a new town. 240 blocks gives a 481 x 481 claim. Applies to new settlements; existing towns keep their saved radius.
wwmc.configuration.maxCitizens.tooltip: Hard citizen cap per town, even after population upgrades. Housing beds are also required. Default: 64.
wwmc.configuration.basePopulation.toolti: Citizen limit before a town buys population upgrades. The town still needs enough housing beds. Default: 10.
How many additional citizens each population upgrade allows, up to Maximum population. Default: 5.
wwmc.configuration.populationUpgradeCost: Emerald price of the first population upgrade. Each later upgrade adds this price again: a value of 8 means costs of 8, 16, 24, and so on.
wwmc.configuration.stationUpgradeCost.to: Emerald price of the first station range or crew upgrade. Each further level doubles the price: a value of 8 means costs of 8, 16 and 32.
wwmc.configuration.quarryWorkers.tooltip: Starting workers per Quarry Station, before crew upgrades. Default: 8.
wwmc.configuration.enchantMinutes.toolti: Base minutes per book or common item. Iron and gold gear take 1.3 times as long, diamond 1.6 times, and netherite twice as long. Rarer items also take longer. Default: 5 minutes.
wwmc.configuration.enchanterMaxLevel.too: Highest enchanting-table level an enchanter can reach, regardless of bookshelves. This is the table level, not the enchantment numeral on an item. Default: 25; level 30 remains for players.
wwmc.configuration.oreVeinSeconds.toolti: Vein replenishment with a stone pickaxe. Better pickaxes shorten the delay, capped at 1.5 times stone speed. Gold ore takes twice as long, diamond and emerald six times, ancient debris eight.
wwmc.configuration.mineMinY.tooltip: Lowest floor Y a new tunnel mine can randomly choose. Default: -30. Existing mine plans keep their saved depth.
wwmc.configuration.mineMaxY.tooltip: Highest floor Y a new tunnel mine can randomly choose. Default: 10. Existing mine plans keep their saved depth.
wwmc.configuration.quarryTargetY.tooltip: Bottom Y for a newly created quarry plan. Bedrock is preserved. Default: -64. Existing quarry plans keep their saved target.
wwmc.configuration.mineBranchLength.tool: Length of each strip-mine side tunnel, in blocks. Default: 24. Applies when a new mine plan is created.
wwmc.configuration.mineBranchPairs.toolt: Number of paired side tunnels along the mine spine, spaced three blocks apart. Default: 4 pairs, or 8 side tunnels. Applies to new mine plans.
wwmc.configuration.workTicks.tooltip: Working ticks needed to harvest a block after reaching it. Lower values make harvesting faster. At the normal tick rate, 20 ticks = 1 second; the default 80 ticks = 4 seconds.
wwmc.configuration.rationTicks.tooltip: Loaded ticks between meals before applying the multiplier. 20 ticks = 1 second. Default base 2400, multiplied by 3, gives one regular meal every 6 minutes. Healing meals have a 30-second cooldown.
wwmc.configuration.alarmThreshold.toolti: Number of hostiles citizens must sight at once before a guard runs to ring the town bell. Individual threats can still call guards without a town-wide alarm. Default: 10.
wwmc.configuration.enemyWaves.tooltip: Enable automatic hostile waves while the settlement owner is home. Turn this off to stop scheduled attacks; ordinary monsters still exist.
wwmc.configuration.waveMinPopulation.too: Minimum citizen population before automatic waves are scheduled. Default: 3 citizens.
wwmc.configuration.waveIntervalDays.tool: Average Minecraft days between automatic waves, with variation of up to 25 percent. Waves arrive at night. Default: 2 days.
wwmc.configuration.waveBaseMobs.tooltip: Enemies in each wave before citizen and population-upgrade scaling. Default: 2.
wwmc.configuration.waveMobsPerCitizen.to: Extra enemies per citizen, rounded up when calculating a wave. Default: 0.5, or roughly one extra enemy per two citizens.
wwmc.configuration.waveMaxMobs.tooltip: Cap on wave size before the extra enemies from population upgrades are added. Upgraded towns can face more than this number. Default: 40.
wwmc.configuration.waveMobsPerUpgrade.to: Extra enemies in every wave for each population upgrade, added above the base wave cap. Upgraded towns also face pillagers, then vindicators from the third upgrade. Default: 2.
wwmc.configuration.maxActiveTraders.tool: Maximum towns with an active trader chunk window in this dimension. Each uses a moving 3x3 area (9 chunks), rather than loading the entire route. Default: 8. Extra traders wait.
wwmc.configuration.tradeRouteDistance.to: Maximum distance between town banners for a trader route. Routes need walkable terrain or roads and remain in the Overworld. Default: 8192 blocks.
wwmc.configuration.randomSettlements.too: Discover small working NPC towns in suitable loaded Overworld terrain. Existing NPC towns remain when this is disabled. They begin neutral, produce real goods, and can accept supply routes.
wwmc.configuration.npcTownSpacing.toolti: Region size used to space candidate towns. Default: 1408 blocks, usually about 1000–2000 blocks between nearby candidates. Terrain and player claims can leave larger gaps. Changing this affects future discoveries.
wwmc.configuration.maxNpcTowns.tooltip: Maximum automatically generated NPC towns in the Overworld. Default: 48; zero prevents new discoveries. This does not remove existing towns.
wwmc.configuration.category.world.toolti: Trader travel limits and discovery of neutral NPC settlements.
wwmc.configuration.mealIntervalMultiplie: Multiplies the base meal interval, including saved settings in existing worlds. Default: 3. The default 2400-tick base becomes 7200 loaded ticks (6 minutes).
wwmc.configuration.fishingSeconds.toolti: Time fishing at a dry bank beside open, two-block-deep water. Default: 30 seconds per whole fish. Butchers prepare catches before cooks can use them.
wwmc.configuration.animalBreeders.toolti: Adult animals preserved in each keeper pen per species. Default: 4. Keepers use real feed and harvest surplus adults. Babies, named animals and mating animals are preserved.
wwmc.configuration.expeditionSites.toolt: Discover finite camps, occupied mines and ruined forts in unclaimed natural terrain.
wwmc.configuration.maxExpeditionSites.to: Keep this many discovered sites, including cleared sites and outposts.
Cap living expedition defenders and convoy raiders, including unloaded defenders.
wwmc.configuration.convoyRaids.tooltip: Nearby occupied camps can warn of and launch raids while players are nearby.
wwmc.configuration.yieldUpgradeCost.tool: First farm or mine yield upgrade price. Each level doubles it: 16, 32 and 64 emeralds by default, for 10%, 20% and 30% average extra produce or mineral drops.
Server logs for sustained worker problems and citizen recovery.
wwmc.configuration.serverDiagnostics.too: Write worker and recovery diagnostics to the server console and latest.log. Default: enabled. Recipe exceptions always log their ID and stack trace.
wwmc.configuration.diagnosticStallSecond: Loaded seconds of a sustained worker problem before its first warning. Default: 120; range: 10 to 3600. Ordinary idle work and off-duty citizens are excluded.
wwmc.configuration.diagnosticRepeatSecon: Minimum seconds between repeat warnings of the same kind for one citizen. Default: 300; range: 30 to 3600. Changing activity or job does not bypass the worker-warning cooldown.
tooltip.wwmc.raw_tin: Smelt raw tin in a furnace to make Tin Ingots.
tooltip.wwmc.tin_ingot: Mix 1 Tin Ingot with 3 Copper Ingots to make 4 Bronze Blends.
tooltip.wwmc.bronze_blend.craft: Craft: 3 Copper Ingots in separate slots + 1 Tin Ingot.
tooltip.wwmc.bronze_blend.smelt: Smelt this blend in a furnace to make a Bronze Ingot.
tooltip.wwmc.bronze_blend.research: Crafting requires your settlement's Bronze Age research.
wwmc.configuration.maxSettlementTraps.to: Maximum placed traps per town. Only traps in ticking chunks activate; each activation spends durability.
